title: But the courtiers who mocked Guido in Or san Michele were in their own house. House of... We don’t want any of your medieval abstrusiosities.
html_source:
It refers to a scene from Boccaccio´s Decameron (Day Sixth, Ninth Novella).
Guido Cavalcanti (1250-1300), a contemporary poet of Dante, is in a cemetery and everyone around him mocks him, to which he replies: “Gentlemen, you can say whatever you like to me, being in your homes”.
Their home is the cemetery because they are going to die and no one will remember them, but it is not Calvanti’s home because, as a poet, he will conquer death.
